result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.select_nodes_by_degree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Select nodes by degree criteria. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L7724-L7794){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.select_nodes_by_degree( min_degree=None, max_degree=None, degree_type="total", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Select nodes by degree](/assets/graphs/select-nodes-by-degree.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Six nodes, each with a badge giving its degree: B and E have degree 3, the others 2. After select_nodes_by_degree with min_degree 3, only B and E are selected and drawn in the accent color." width="100%"} Filters nodes based on their degree (number of connections). Useful for finding hubs (high degree) or peripheral nodes (low degree). Can filter by in-degree, out-degree, or total degree. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [min_degree]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Minimum degree threshold (inclusive). `None` means no lower bound. [max_degree]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum degree threshold (inclusive). `None` means no upper bound. [degree_type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["total"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Type of degree to use: `"in"`, `"out"`, or `"total"`. For undirected graphs, only `"total"` is valid. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a 10-node star, the hub has degree `10` while every spoke has degree `1`, so a `min_degree=5` filter selects only the hub: ::: {#091033dd .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_star_graph(10) .select_nodes_by_degree(min_degree=5) ) len(graph.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: Combining `min_degree` and `max_degree` selects a band of degrees -- here, nodes with 1 or 2 outgoing edges in a directed path: ::: {#7a29f8f8 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_path_graph(10) .select_nodes_by_degree(min_degree=1, max_degree=2, degree_type="out") ) len(graph.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 9 ``` ::: :::
